title: docs(rest): the `'platform'` virtual-id docblock names the live `/environments/` URL family
body:
Fixes #15858

Clause-②: no

## What this is

`RestServer`'s `environmentId === 'platform'` docblock described the reserved virtual id as being addressed *"through the regular project URL shape (`/projects/platform/...`)"* — the spelling ADR-0006 v4's second addendum (D2, executed 2026-08-28) retired with **no alias and no grace period**. It now reads *"through the regular environment URL shape (`/environments/platform/...`)"*.

Comment-only. Two lines change; the file is line-count neutral at **13,877 lines before and after**.

```diff
-     * by Studio to address the control plane through the regular project
-     * URL shape (`/projects/platform/...`). It is NOT a row in the projects
+     * by Studio to address the control plane through the regular environment
+     * URL shape (`/environments/platform/...`). It is NOT a row in the projects
```

## Why the prefix is corrected and the paragraph is NOT retired

The card opened an explicit fork — *"if the shape is live the sentence needs its prefix corrected, and if it is not, the paragraph may want retiring rather than transliterating"* — and held its second half behind a cross-repo reading. That reading came back (#15861, comment `5683109868`): **the shape is live**, addressed under the `/environments/` spelling. The host enables environment scoping precisely so `/api/v1/environments/platform/...` resolves to the control-plane protocol; its kernel resolver returns no per-environment kernel for that id; a live pin drives `routePath: '/environments/platform/meta'`. Framework-side, this file's own `resolveProtocol` still short-circuits `environmentId === 'platform'` to the control-plane protocol.

So every behavioural claim in the paragraph is true today, on both sides of the seam. Only the URL spelling and the phrase "the regular project URL shape" were not — which is exactly the prefix-correction arm, the same shape as the half PR #16543 already landed.

## What was measured, not assumed

**How many sites are left, and by what predicate.** Located by symbol, never by line — the line numbers in this card's family have drifted repeatedly (the reading seat named `:1788-1794` / `:4623`; the PM measured `:1841` / `:4674`; both were right on their own day). Predicate: a `projects` URL-shaped path literal in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` — **2 hits**, one of which is correct and stays. Widened to `packages/rest` (src + test) it is **3 hits**; the third is the same correct sentence in `discovery-per-request-protocol.test.ts`. Line-wrapping hides two of the card's own quoted phrases from a naive grep, so the sweep was re-run over comment text with the wrapping joined.

**Zero-hit control.** A zero here is a trap this card has already sprung once: the literal token `projects/:id` returns **0** on `origin/main` while the real spellings are `/projects/platform/...` and `/projects/:environmentId`. Every zero below carries a same-subject control word known to be present: `/environments` occurs **31** times in this file and `project` occurs **101** times, so the grep can see this family.

**`skip-changeset` was measured, not assumed.** `packages/rest` publishes `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`. The tsup DTS rollup preserves this docblock, so it ships: before the edit `projects/platform` appeared in **4** published files (`dist/index.js`, `dist/index.cjs`, `dist/index.d.ts`, `dist/index.d.cts`, at `index.d.ts:536`); after it appears in **0**, and `environments/platform` appears in the same 4. Published bytes move, so this takes a **`patch`** changeset rather than the label.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, noted and not filed here

1. ⭐ **The docblock this PR corrects is DETACHED — it documents `resolveProtocol` from a position where nothing binds it.** At `rest-server.ts:1825-1846` it is immediately followed by a second block comment (`:1847-1853`) that binds to `resolveHostnameCached`, so TSDoc attaches the *nearer* one and this paragraph documents no declaration at all. `resolveProtocol` has its own, newer docblock at `:1930-1948`. That is very likely how the stale spelling survived a rename sweep: the text is invisible where a reader of the method would look for it, and it still ships in `dist/index.d.ts`. ⛔ Not repaired here — re-attaching or deleting it is a different class from this card's spelling fix, and the card's own fork was decided for transliteration.
2. **The detached block's numbered resolution chain is incomplete.** It lists hostname → header → default-project → control-plane, while `resolveRequestEnvironmentId` now tries the host-injected `RestRequestEnvResolver` seam (ADR-0076 D11 step ④) *first*. The method's own bound docblock at `:1863-1874` states the current chain correctly. Same paragraph-position problem as note 1, and not a claim about the `'platform'` special case this card is graded on.
3. **The same paragraph's *"It is NOT a row in the projects table"*** is about a table, not a URL, and is deliberately untouched. The reading seat flagged it and declined to answer it rather than guess it into the edit. One in-repo datum toward whoever picks it up: `packages/spec` consistently names the cloud control plane's environment row **`sys_environment`** (`discovery.zod.ts:414`, `platform-object-names.ts:151`), so the sentence is plausibly stale too — but the authority is the cloud repository, and this seat did not measure it there.
4. **The sibling sites that call `/projects/:environmentId` "the retired spelling" are correct and untouched** (`rest-server.ts:4674`, `discovery-per-request-protocol.test.ts:359`) — they document the repair that landed under #16538. Harmonising the two directions would have made the right one wrong.

Filed as #18353 / #18348, so no new card.
